exercise.name: Barbell Lying Triceps Extension Skull Crusher

reference.title: Barbell Lying Triceps Extension Skull Crusher
reference.listing: Video (title from the listing URL; the page could not be fetched from this environment, so the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)

breathing.pattern: Inhale as the bar lowers toward the forehead, exhale as the elbows straighten.
breathing.cadence: About 2.2 s down, short pause, about 1.4 s up

prescription.load: Barbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can control for every rep with 1-3 reps in reserve (RPE 7-9).
prescription.progression: More reps in the range, then 1-2.5 kg more, then a slower lowering

cues.text: Lie on a flat bench, feet flat on the floor. Hold the bar overhand, hands about shoulder width or a little narrower, arms straight up over the shoulders.
Breathe in and bend only the elbows: the bar travels in an arc down toward the forehead.
Bar just above the forehead, upper arms still, elbows pointing at the ceiling and about shoulder width apart.
Breathe out and straighten the elbows, moving only the forearms.
Arms straight but not locked over the shoulders; repeat.

mistakes.mistake: Upper arms swinging back and forth (turning it into a pullover)
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbows pointing at the ceiling; only the forearms move.
Keep the elbows about shoulder width apart.

mistakes.mistake: Dropping the bar onto the head
mistakes.fix: Lower under control and stop just above the forehead; use a lighter bar if control slips.

mistakes.mistake: Lower back arching off the bench
mistakes.fix: Brace, keep the feet planted and the ribs down.

mistakes.mistake: Wrists bending back under the bar
mistakes.fix: Keep the wrists straight; an EZ bar can be easier on the wrists.

kinematics.norm: About shoulder width or a little narrower (clinical opinion)

Straight but not locked at the top; lower until the bar is just above the forehead, about 100-120 degrees of elbow flexion (clinical opinion). Activation and relative force were matched across the three heads at 90 degrees of flexion or more (PLoS ONE 2021)
Upper arms about vertical (about 90 degrees of shoulder flexion) and still; at 90 degrees and above the medial head carries the most force (Kholinne 2018)
The bar stops just above the forehead and never touches the face (clinical opinion)
Feet flat on the floor with the knees bent about 90 degrees (clinical opinion)
Controlled, about 2 s lowering and 1-1.5 s pressing (clinical opinion); the EMG comparison used sets of 7 reps at 70% of 1RM (Boehler 2011)

sources.title: GymVisual, Barbell Lying Triceps Extension Skull Crusher, video (movement reference)

Boehler 2011, electromyographic analysis of the triceps brachii muscle during a variety of triceps exercises (MS thesis, University of Wisconsin-La Crosse, ACE-sponsored; 15 women, 8 exercises at 70% 1RM)

The different role of each head of the triceps brachii muscle in elbow extension (Acta Orthop Traumatol Turc 2018;52(3):201-205; PubMed 29503079; EMG plus OpenSim at 0-180 degrees of shoulder elevation)
Effect of elbow joint angles on electromyographic activity versus force relationships of synergistic muscles of the triceps brachii (PLoS ONE 2021; PMC8174684)

cautions: The bar travels toward the face: start light, lower slowly, and use a spotter for heavy sets (clinical opinion).
Elbow pain: shorten the range or switch to dumbbells or an EZ bar (clinical opinion).
Take the bar from a spotter or press it up from the chest; never swing it over the face.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Wrist discomfort: an EZ bar or dumbbells (neutral grip).
Elbow discomfort: lower to the top of the head instead (less elbow bend).
progressions: Pause just above the forehead (1 s).

muscleNotes.triceps_r: Does all of the work: lowers the bar under control and straightens the elbows. In the lying barbell triceps extension the long and lateral heads differed in activity (Boehler 2011). With the upper arm vertical the medial head produced the most force in a model and EMG study (Kholinne 2018).
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Does all of the work: lowers the bar under control and straightens the elbows. In the lying barbell triceps extension the long and lateral heads differed in activity (Boehler 2011). With the upper arm vertical the medial head produced the most force in a model and EMG study (Kholinne 2018).
muscleNotes.lats_r: Hold the upper arms vertical as the bar travels toward the head (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.lats_l: Hold the upper arms vertical as the bar travels toward the head (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Helps the lats keep the elbows pointing at the ceiling (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_l: Helps the lats keep the elbows pointing at the ceiling (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Grip the bar and keep the wrists straight.
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Grip the bar and keep the wrists straight.
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the ribs down and the lower back from arching off the bench.
